ledger.x: 9 November 1799: the coup of 18 Brumaire makes Bonaparte First Consul.
November 1799: the Helvetic Republic stays France's client.
8 March 1801: the British land at Aboukir.
27 June 1801: Cairo and the Nile valley are lost.
2 September 1801: the fighting in Egypt ends with the capitulation of Alexandria; 'the campaign ultimately ended in failure, with 15,000 French troops killed in action and 15,000 by disease'.
1802: Parma and Piacenza fall to France in fact.
19 February 1803: the Helvetic Republic is abolished.
18 May 1804: the Consulate gives way to the Empire.

wars.name: French campaign in Egypt and Syria
wars.outcome: The French held Cairo and Lower Egypt from 1798 and reached Girga in Upper Egypt on 29 December 1798; Bonaparte left in August 1799; Kléber signed the Convention of El Arish on 24 January 1800 (rejected by Britain); the British landed on 8 March 1801…

wars.name: Marengo campaign and Treaty of Lunéville
wars.outcome: Victory at Marengo on 14 June 1800; the Treaty of Lunéville of 9 February 1801 ceded the left bank of the Rhine to France, recognised the Cisalpine, Ligurian, Batavian and Helvetic republics and confirmed Austria in Venetia and Istria.

certainty.note: French frontiers on the Rhine, in the Alps and in Italy follow treaty lines (Lunéville 1801) and the annexed départements.
